title: Full n-Bit Security and Nonce-Misuse Resistance for Block-Cipher MACs
summary: Some nonce-based block-cipher MACs achieve three-quarters of n bits of PRF security, but full n-bit security with nonce-misuse resistance remains open.

formal_statement.body: Prior nonce-based block cipher-based MAC constructions using two block cipher calls, one universal hash-function call, and an arbitrary number of XOR operations have been analyzed in the faulty-nonce model; some achieve $3n/4$-bit PRF security, but the tightness of those constructions remains open. The unresolved construction-existence question is whether a nonce-based block cipher-based MAC construction can provide both full $n$-bit security and nonce misuse resistance. [S1]

scope.domain: Design and PRF security of nonce-based block-cipher MACs in the faulty-nonce model.
assumptions: PRF security is analyzed in the faulty-nonce model.
parameters: n: target security level measured in bits
Two block-cipher calls, one universal hash-function call, and arbitrary XOR operations: resource profile of the prior constructions
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a nonce-based block-cipher MAC can provide full n-bit security and nonce-misuse resistance; the tightness of the constructions achieving three-quarters of n bits of PRF security also remains open.

citations.label: Toward Full n-bit Security and Nonce Misuse Resistance of Block Cipher-based MACs

progress.summary: The source notes that some prior nonce-based constructions achieve three-quarters of n bits of PRF security while their tightness remains open. It then explicitly asks whether full n-bit security and nonce-misuse resistance can be achieved together.
citation_labels: Wonseok Choi et al., Toward Full n-bit Security and Nonce Misuse Resistance of Block Cipher-based MACs
